patients.summary: Operations manager with long-standing hypertension who joins the practice in 2017; ADPKD found in 2020, then psychogenic ED, an adjustment disorder, aortic regurgitation with an ascending aneurysm, flutter-driven cardiomyopathy that recovers after ablation, stage III follicular lymphoma treated to remission, and an aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage in March 2026.

documents.title: New patient inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is looking for a new primary care doctor; his previous office is reducing hours and he wants somewhere he can reach the doctor directly. Explained membership and how insurance still applies for labs and specialists. Has high blood pressure, on two pills. Booked new patient physical 6/21 at 8:00. Release form emailed so we can request his old records.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every morning

documents.title: New Patient Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
42M establishing care. Previous PCP office cutting back, wants more access.

HTN: told about 5 yrs ago after a run of high readings at a work health fair. On lisinopril 20 and HCTZ 25 for several years, takes them in the morning, rarely misses. Doesn't check at home. No HA, CP, SOB, edema.

PMH: HTN. No surgeries. No hospitalizations.
Meds: lisinopril 20 mg daily, HCTZ 25 mg daily. No supplements.
All: NKDA.
FH: father had kidney disease and eventually a kidney transplant, pt not sure of the details. Paternal grandfather died at 58 of bleeding in the brain. Mother: HTN, high cholesterol.
SH: married. Senior operations manager at a manufacturing/distribution company, there about 10 yrs, long days. Never smoker. Alcohol 2-3 drinks a week, social. No drugs. Walks some on weekends.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: BP 138/88 (repeat similar), HR 70, SpO2 98%. Ht 180 cm, wt 88 kg.
Well appearing. HEENT unremarkable, fundi not visualized well without dilation. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses felt. Ext without edema. Skin no worrisome lesions. Neuro grossly normal.

A/P
1. HTN - borderline on two drugs. Ask him to buy a home cuff and send readings. Continue lisinopril/HCTZ. CMP.
2. Health maintenance - CBC, CMP, lipids, UA, hep C screen (never done). Tdap - doesn't remember last one, will check old records. Flu in the fall.
3. Records release signed.

RTC 6 months for BP, sooner with readings.

documents.title: Visit summary
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Today: new patient physical. Your blood pressure was 138/88; goal is under 130/80. Please buy an upper-arm home cuff and send two weeks of morning readings through the portal. Keep taking lisinopril 20 mg and hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg each morning. Blood and urine tests were sent; results in a few days.

documents.title: Results from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Glenn, labs look good overall. Kidney function, potassium and blood counts are normal and the hepatitis C screen is negative. Your triglycerides are high and LDL is borderline; less alcohol, fewer refined carbs and more walking would help both. We'll recheck in a year. Send me some home blood pressure readings when you have the cuff.

events.reason: records from prior primary care office

documents.title: Prior primary care records
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: 42 pages received from previous primary care office (2009-2017). Scanned to media tab.

documents.title: Review of prior records
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed old chart. HTN diagnosed 2012 after elevated readings; on lisinopril and HCTZ since. Creatinine 1.0-1.1 across the years, potassium normal. Lipids similar to ours, no statin discussed. Tdap 2007, so due next physical. No colon screening yet (too young then). Flu shots most years. Nothing else of note.

documents.title: BP numbers
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got the cuff. Two weeks of mornings: mostly 132-140 over 84-90, one 146/92 after a bad night's sleep. Is that ok?

documents.title: RE: BP numbers
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks Glenn. A little higher than I'd like (goal under 130/80). Keep the salt down and the walking up, and let's look again at your visit in December before we change anything.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Quadrivalent flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. No prior reactions. VIS given. Tolerated, left before his 8:30 meeting.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: HTN follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
BP f/u. Home readings run 130s-140s/high 80s. Busy quarter at work, eating out a lot. Taking both meds. No side effects.
Exam: BP as recorded, HR regular. Heart RRR no murmur, lungs clear, no edema.
A/P: HTN, near goal but not at it. He'd rather work on diet and walking before adding a third drug. Continue lisinopril 20/HCTZ 25. Recheck at physical in June.

documents.title: Refill: lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy requested 90-day supplies of lisinopril 20 mg and HCTZ 25 mg. Last BP visit 12/2017, last BMP 6/2017. Sent per protocol with 1 refill each.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Feels well. Work still heavy, travel to the distribution sites twice a month. Walks the dog, not much else. Alcohol unchanged.
Home BP 130s-140s/80s.
Meds lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25. NKDA.
ROS negative.
Exam: BP 141/86, rest of vitals fine. Normal general exam; heart without murmur, lungs clear, abdomen benign, no edema.
A/P
- HTN: running a bit above goal. Discussed adding amlodipine vs tightening lifestyle; he prefers lifestyle another 6 months. Continue current.
- Lipids: recheck today.
- Tdap today (last 2007).
- Colon screening at 50.
RTC December.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kidney function and potassium are normal on the blood pressure pills. Triglycerides still elevated and LDL about the same as last year. Nothing to start; keep at the diet changes.

documents.title: Outside flu vaccine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy notification: quadrivalent influenza vaccine given 10/10/2018. Entered into immunization record.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: BP check
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Lunchtime visit. Cut back on takeout since the fall, lost a little. Home numbers mid-130s/mid-80s. Feels fine.
BP 138/88 today, HR normal. Heart and lungs normal, no edema.
HTN slightly above goal, trending better. Continue lisinopril/HCTZ. Physical in summer with labs.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
44M annual. No new complaints. Taking meds daily. Home BP he hasn't checked in a few months.
NKDA. FH/SH unchanged.
Exam: BP 144/91, weight down slightly. Normal exam: lungs clear, heart regular without murmur, abdomen soft, no edema, skin clear.
A/P
1. HTN - still a touch high. Back to home readings, send 2 wks. Continue.
2. Labs today.
3. Colonoscopy: guidance moving to 45; will plan in the next couple of years.
4. Flu in the fall.

documents.title: Your labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All stable from last year: normal kidney function, blood counts and liver tests. Triglycerides still on the high side. Still waiting on those home BP numbers when you get a chance.

documents.title: Flu vaccine and BP check
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine given R deltoid, tolerated. BP checked at his request after a stressful day, 150/96 seated. Says he never sent home readings. Reminded him; PCP aware.
